thread_text:
Marta: quick flag 1: ran lynx-embed-v1 int5 bringup. aggregate recall@10 OK on head but tail is fragile. need quick triage.
Diego: drop the core numbers and export settings?
Marta: paste: `backend=onnx, quant=per_channel_int5, calib_method=uniform_max, clamp=max, fold_ln=true`
Marta: results small table:
```
model                 recall@10  recall@1  tail_recall@10  silhouette
prod-embed-v3         0.806      0.413     0.291           0.36
lynx-embed-v1-int5    0.768      0.398     0.204           0.19
```
Leah: tail_recall down ~8.7% absolute. that's significant for niche search.
Jin: did you try per-dim calibration (collect activations per-layer and compute per-dim scales)? int5 often needs that.
Marta: not yet. we used quick uniform calibration to save time.
Diego: also check export folding. folding LN + quant can shift embedding norm distribution. try `fold_ln=false`.
Marta: ok rerunning with per-dim calib + clamp=99.9pct + fold_ln=false. kicking eval-bot for per-topic CSV and kNN components.
eval-bot: job 79001 queued for lynx-embed-v1-int5. ETA 6m.
Marta: while that's running, small probe: compute cosine norm drift between prod and quantized vectors (sample 50k head, 50k tail).
Leah: useful metric: fraction of pairs whose cosine drops >0.05 compared to float. tail should be inspected separately.
Jin: also compute kNN component size distribution (k=8). If there are many components size 1-5 it's fragmentation.
infra-bot: FYI staging canary slice ready (5% traffic) if you want to A/B. need PR for rollout policy.
Marta: good to know. will hold canary until we confirm metrics.
eval-bot: job 79001 completed. summary:
- tail_recall@10 = 0.246 (improved from 0.204)
- recall@10 overall = 0.783
- silhouette = 0.27
- knn_components_k8: mean_comp_size=14, num_components=12 (prod mean=50, num=4)
- cosine_drop_fraction_tail = 0.12
details CSV: https://internal/redwood-evals/79001.csv
Leah: per-dim calib + percentile clamp helped a lot (tail_recall +4.2%). silhouette also improved. still not prod parity.
Diego: consider trying per-channel int6 as a fall-back; cost delta vs int5 is modest but quality might be much closer.
Jin: agree. run int6 per-channel and also try `quant_backend=tvm` to see if kernels differ. some backends use symmetric quant vs asymmetric which can affect micro-shifts.
Marta: I'll queue int6 per-channel + tvm run. also export artifacts and put the ONNX proto in embed-onboard/artifacts.
infra-bot: note: tvm runs currently on nodes x3-x5, might queue ~10m.
Marta: queued job 79002 for lynx int6, per-channel.
eval-bot: job 79002 finished. quick recap:
- lynx-int6-perchannel recall@10 = 0.798, tail_recall@10 = 0.278, silhouette = 0.33
- latency +2% vs int5, memory +6% (still below int8 by ~10%)
CSV: https://internal/redwood-evals/79002.csv
Leah: int6 per-channel is much closer to prod. silhouette nearly matches.
Diego: decision time: either accept int6 per-channel for staging canary or keep iterating on int5 (more engineering to tune calibration). cost analysis?
Marta: int6 increases cost ~7% vs int5 but reduces tail misses significantly. My recommendation: go int6 for initial canary, continue low-priority work to harden int5 calibration.
Jin: +1. We should also add a weighted tail metric to SLO dashboard (tail_weight=3) so product impact is tracked.
Leah: I'll open an eval ticket to add weighted_recall to per-deploy checks.
Marta: PR'ing artifact drop and canary PR now. will post canary results in this thread.
Diego: thanks. small note: archive these CSVs under embed-onboard/evals/lynx for future regression traces.
Marta: done. thanks team.
